summary: Duplicate function/tool executions when mixing Go gRPC client and TS HTTP client: idempotency header encoding mismatch
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports duplicate downstream tool/function executions when a multi-service orchestrator mixes a Go gRPC client and a TypeScript HTTP client in the same session. Root cause appears related to different encodings/metadata keys used by gRPC (binary metadata) versus HTTP (text header) across our edge proxies.

Impact: Multiple customers using mixed-language orchestrators (Go + TS) see duplicated external webhook/tool calls on retries. Duplicates cause side effects (duplicate database writes, external webhook POSTs) and have led to one customer to temporarily disable automated retries.

Observed start: 2026-03-11 22:10 UTC. Reported via customer support ticket and linked Slack (#support-datasilo).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Setup an orchestrator with two client processes: a Go microservice using our Go gRPC SDK to call /v1/stream (gRPC) and a TypeScript worker using the HTTP SDK to call the same session via REST.
2) From TypeScript worker, send a function/tool-invocation request with idempotency key header 'x-redwood-idempotency' (text).
3) From Go gRPC client, send a matching request concurrently but the Go SDK attaches metadata key 'x-redwood-idempotency-bin' as binary metadata (raw bytes).
4) Induce a transient network error at the gateway (tcp reset) to force client-side retry of the TypeScript HTTP call.
5) Observe duplicated tool execution downstream (two webhook POSTs) despite both clients thinking they used the same idempotency value.
logs: customer-observed: two webhook POSTs to https://hooks.datasilo.com/processor within 200ms of the retry attempt

proxy-translation: grpc-proxy normalized '-bin' metadata into base64 string 'QjFmNGMyYjA...' and attached header 'x-redwood-idempotency: QjFmNGMyYjA...' while HTTP client used raw UUID string 'B1f4c2b0-9e7a-4'
serving-runtime trace: session_id=ses_03a2, trace_id=tr_9c4; tool_exec_id first=tool_112, second=tool_113; both had different idempotency canonical values, so dedupe check missed.
comments: 2026-03-12 08:15 - Jordan Phillips (Support): Logged from customer call; they can reproduce reliably when Go and TS clients participate in same session. Provided sample traces and webhook timestamps.

2026-03-12 09:02 - Lina Ortiz (SRE): Investigating. Initial hypothesis: gRPC '-bin' metadata is base64-encoded by the proxy; HTTP client sends plain text UUID. Gateway dedupe logic compares canonical header string and does not decode base64 '-bin' equivalently.

2026-03-12 11:40 - DataSilo (Customer): We confirmed two identical downstream POST bodies and different idempotency values in logs. We had to disable retries to avoid duplicates; this is blocking our production pipeline.

2026-03-12 14:20 - Lina Ortiz (SRE): Temporary customer workaround: prefer consistent surface (both clients use HTTP or both use gRPC) or ensure Go SDK uses text header encoding (workaround patch attached). Will prepare gateway fix to canonicalize both encodings.

2026-03-13 07:30 - Eng (Gateway): Created draft PR to change gateway dedupe to decode '-bin' metadata into UTF-8 when possible, and to fallback to hex/base64 normalization. See PR #1284. Need security review for binary-to-text conversions.

2026-03-13 16:10 - Support (Jordan): Sent customer recommended temporary SDK patch for Go to set header 'x-redwood-idempotency' as text in addition to metadata (double-send) to avoid mismatch. Customer accepted patch; re-enabled retries under observation.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: mismatch between 'x-redwood-idempotency' (text) and 'x-redwood-idempotency-bin' (binary) resulted in different canonical values downstream; dedupe only matched exact header string.

Reproduced in staging by running concurrent TS HTTP and Go gRPC clients against edge-proxy with tcpkill induced transient resets. Confirmed two executions when binary metadata encoded as base64 differs from raw text UUID.

Examined gateway code path: grpc-proxy currently leaves '-bin' metadata as base64 without attempting reversible decoding into UTF-8 text; compare logic uses strict string equality against HTTP header value.
Security note: decoding arbitrary binary metadata into UTF-8 for canonicalization could be unsafe; need to whitelist expected idempotency header formats (UUID, hex, base64 of UTF-8).

Tested local gateway patch that normalizes both forms: 1) if header present and looks like UUID, use that; 2) if '-bin' present, attempt base64 decode and validate UTF-8/UUID; 3) compare normalized tokens for dedupe. Patch passes unit tests and reproducer.
resolution:
Workaround delivered: customer applied a small Go SDK patch (attached) that sets both the text header 'x-redwood-idempotency' and the binary metadata 'x-redwood-idempotency-bin' with identical byte/UTF-8 encoding; after that, duplicates stopped.

Planned permanent fix: gateway PR #1284 will add normalization to accept and compare both text and -bin metadata by canonicalizing to UTF-8/UUID when safe. Security review scheduled and a canary rollout to prod us-east by 2026-03-18.

Follow-ups: update SDK docs with cross-language idempotency guidance, add an integration test in e2e suite that mixes gRPC and HTTP clients, and add a monitoring alert for duplicate tool executions per session above threshold.
